report.source_text: Abdominopelvic computer tomographic scan (CT-Scan) without contrast showed enlarged kidneys with the renal parenchyma replaced by innumerable cyst of varying sizes. The right kidney was ectopically located in the right aspect of the pelvis. The right and left kidneys measure 18.8 cm × 8.0 cm and 21 cm × 9.8 cm respectively. The cysts were hypodense with thin walls with some of the walls calcified. The other intra-abdominal organs did not have cysts (Figs. 2, 3 and 4).

clinician.final_diagnosis: Autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease with right pelvic ectopic multicystic kidney
clinician.trajectory_summary: A 46-year-old Ghanaian male presented with painless total hematuria and left flank dull pain, and elevated blood pressure. Abdominal ultrasound showed enlarged kidneys with multiple cysts of varying sizes and a right kidney ectopically located in the right iliac fossa. Renal function tests revealed marked impairment with creatinine 518 μmol/l and eGFR 13 ml/min. CT scan confirmed enlarged kidneys with numerous cysts replacing the renal parenchyma and ectopic right pelvic kidney with calcified cyst walls. No other abdominal organs were affected.
